RE-MEASURED THE SAME DAY, ON THE SAME DOCUMENT, AFTER THE CAUSE IT DIAGNOSED WAS FIXED. Its table is now the BEFORE column: total to queryable 8,828 ms -> 909 ms, import 8,398 ms -> 705 ms, on 3,140 nodes / 13,390 edges, release, in-memory backend, no full-text index.

WHICH PART MOVED: the numbers, and the superlinearity. The O(E^1.7) shape was caused by a linear scan of the write buffer on every buffered read, which is gone — the buffer carries a BTreeMap index over its own ops now, so a lookup is a range/point query rather than a walk.

WHICH PART STILL STANDS, and is the reason this is an INVALIDATES rather than a closure: the observation's HEADLINE was that the byte store is not the bottleneck, measured with no byte store present at all. That is not only still true, it is more firmly true — the remaining 705 ms is serialization, schema validation and puts, none of it storage. Its bounds also still stand: the full-text index was off, so every figure on both sides of this comparison is a lower bound for a hydrate that must answer search_design.

⚠️ AND ITS DIAGNOSIS OF THE MECHANISM WAS WRONG, which the node should not be read for. It attributed the superlinearity to adjacency lists being read-modify-write per edge insert. Reading the code killed that: adj_out_key includes the target id, so every edge is its own key — three puts, no reads. The cost was on the READ side. chg:write-buffer-gets-an-index-and-hydrate-drops-tenfold carries the correct account.

🛑 NOT FOUND BY unclaimed_findings, and worth knowing why: that computation reached subjects_examined=1 (cmp:byte-store, what the ChangeEvent touched) and returned nothing, because this observation's subject_id is a Decision. The change and the finding hang off different nodes, so nothing joined them. Closed by judgement instead — an empty shortlist is not evidence that nothing went stale.
